title: ProjectE boot observability report
description: Output of tools/scripts/board/boot_observability.py. Answers the question a bring-up bench asks first: the board does not boot, which rail failed? Crosses rail_budget's enable graph against testpoint_plan's scope. 'checks_physical_access' is pinned false - there is no placement here, and testpoint_plan.py already draws that line with phase: early_schematic / physical: null.

checks_physical_access.description: Checks the SCOPE of the test-point plan, never whether a pad is reachable by a probe. Placement does not exist at this phase.

power_up_tiers.description: From railbudget.enable_order. Rails inside one tier come up together - the graph does not order them, and that is exactly where ambiguity can hide.

kind.description: NO DEFAULT. A power-good pin counted as a rail measurement is the error this distinction exists to prevent: a regulator can assert PG into a rail held down by a downstream short.

proves_rail.description: True only when a rail_voltage observation exists. PG and enable observations are real information about something else.

failure_classes.description: The metric that matters. Rails whose failures produce the same observable state sit in one class; a class with more than one member is two faults nobody can tell apart. Counting 'rails with test points' instead reads well and hides exactly this.

resets.description: Reported apart from the rails because the symptom differs: a reset released before its rails are up gives a powered, dead board, which looks nothing like a missing rail.

enable_edges.description: Enable sources that are themselves invisible. Information rather than a failure: an enable is usually the output of an observable rail, and measuring that rail already says whether the gate opened.

diagnosability.description: Both numbers are reported on purpose: '5 rails, 5 classes' and '5 rails, 2 classes' are very different boards, and a single coverage percentage makes them look similar.
